clue.text: Orchestra getting pounds, allowing little expense externally - it may have some beaming

indicators.note: something placed externally sits outside, so the stingy word wraps round the others

blocks.note: L is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A thrifty orchestra trying to keep its spending down while still putting on a bright show.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight means stingy, the opposite of lavish spending; the definition is a cryptic hint at a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light thrown from a hand-held lamp is a beam, so the whole definition describes what such illumination contains.

clue.text: Dreamland, wrapped in many sheets? On the contrary

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped up inside the first word of the clue, its letters running unbroken
this flips the stated relation: the sheets are not around the word, the word is around the sheets

blocks.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: A dreamer tucked up under a heap of bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue says Dreamland lies inside many sheets; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so the sheets lie inside Dreamland: dREAMland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, traditionally five hundred leaves, so a large stack of them.

clue.text: No brave supplier of witticism will get punishment

blocks.note: a card is an amusing joker, a wag

explanation.surface: A cowardly joker is warned that a penalty awaits him.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is old-fashioned slang for a comic person, someone always cracking jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee shows this caution to a player as a disciplinary sanction for foul play.

clue.text: Case one truck picked up

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a ute is a utility vehicle, a small pickup truck

explanation.surface: A single lorry is collected, presumably containing a case.
explanation.walkthrough: I then UTE, read upwards, gives ETUI.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental holder for needles, pins or cosmetics, a dainty kind of box.

clue.text: US city is trying out restriction on speech?

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Los Angeles is experimenting with curbing free expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restriction on speech' sounds like censorship; the question mark warns it is literal, a throat condition that limits talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box leaves a sufferer hoarse or voiceless, physically limiting the ability to talk.

clue.text: Facilities supporting South East European

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means lying underneath, so that piece comes second

blocks.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet; lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: Plumbing built for someone from southeastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are the peoples speaking Slavic languages, found across eastern and central parts of the continent, Russians, Poles, Czechs and others.

clue.text: Those in first rose excitedly to welcome writer

indicators.note: something done excitedly is agitated and jumbled, so the flower word is rearranged
welcoming someone means taking them in, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A rose bloom eagerly greets an author.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen are the two who go in first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's opening batsmen, or the first acts or games on a bill, are those who go in at the start.

clue.text: Almost certain to deliver an end to fighting

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: a word for certain, missing its final letter
render means hand over or give

explanation.surface: A diplomat feels sure they can bring about a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its E, then RENDER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up to an enemy is how one side concludes hostilities, so capitulation brings combat to a close.

clue.text: Problem swapping sources of suitable covering?

indicators.note: sources are the starts of words, so the opening letters of the two words change places

blocks.note: fit means suitable and a pall is a cloth draped over a coffin; exchange the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A puzzle about exchanging the origins of an appropriate cover.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT PALL with initial letters exchanged becomes PIT FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or unexpected difficulty, a trap one stumbles into.

clue.text: Request no second vegetable

indicators.note: the word loses whichever letter stands in second place

explanation.surface: Asking for no second helping of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: PLEA without its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a small round green seed eaten as a common garden legume.

clue.text: Desert transport turned up late at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: The ride across the sands arrived behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' tempts a reversal; here it simply means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is the classic beast of burden used to ride or carry goods across arid sandy regions.

clue.text: Broadcast a very little, ignoring the French type of programme

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are removed
broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Transmitting barely anything, with no French content.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LE out of A VERY LITTLE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality television is a genre of unscripted shows following ordinary people, a recognised category of broadcast.

clue.text: Instruction to head for port resulted in evidence of damage, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: as in an injury left a mark
a weal is a raised mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A ship turning to port bumped something and came away scarred.
explanation.walkthrough: Left wheel is a drill or steering command to turn to the left; port is the left side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is the left-hand side, so a command to swing that way tells the helmsman or column to turn left.

clue.text: Give indication of supporting heads rolling with pained expression

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over, so the letters of the word before are tumbled into new order

explanation.surface: A grim scene at an execution, heads tumbling while onlookers wince.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to hint at or presage something that is yet to come, offering a sign in advance.

clue.text: Inclining to dismiss a brilliant historic city

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the single letter named is removed from the word before

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to write off a splendid old city.
explanation.walkthrough: LEANING drops its A; Leningrad was the Soviet name for St Petersburg, hence historic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city of St Petersburg bore this Soviet-era name from 1924 to 1991, so it is a former name.

clue.text: Instrument problem borders on laughable

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: a bug is a fault or snag

explanation.surface: A musician's trouble with their instrument verges on the ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass horn without valves, used chiefly for military signals.

clue.text: Name encountered in Scottish island has to do with Lakeland location

indicators.note: something met in a place is found inside it, so the first piece goes within the island

blocks.note: a term is a word used to name something
Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A name met on a Scottish island turns out to be connected with the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District in north-west England; the island's last letter stays outside the inserted name.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttermere is one of the lakes, and a village beside it, in Cumbria's Lake District, so a place there.

clue.text: Anger, being cut up over wreck of spare tyre (emptied)

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top
a wreck is something smashed apart, so the letters of the following word are broken up and rebuilt
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone furious at being mocked about their wobbly midriff, the spare tyre of fat round the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed AXE above the rest: EXA, then ASPER, then TE. A spare tyre is a roll of belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate someone is to irritate or infuriate them intensely, so the verb anger fits.

clue.text: Rebuffed newspaper to bring down former film star

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests pushed back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
to land an aircraft is to bring it down

explanation.surface: A spurned tabloid sets out to topple a fading Hollywood celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG reversed is GAR, then LAND. Judy Garland starred in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy Garland was a Hollywood actress and singer of the 1930s to 1960s, now dead, so a past screen star.

clue.text: Register inaccurate citation, ignoring chapter

indicators.note: chapter abbreviates to a single letter, which is left out of the word
inaccurate means not right, so the remaining letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An academic flags a wrong reference, minus its chapter number.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from CITATION and rearrange. Notitia is a rare word, chiefly for an ecclesiastical list or register.
explanation.definitionFit: A notitia is a catalogue or roll, especially of church dioceses or officials, so a formal list.

clue.text: Some into sedition should be drawn out

indicators.note: only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Anyone dabbling in rebellion ought to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: inTO SEDition. Tose is a dialect word meaning to tease out or card wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To tose is to pull or tease fibres apart, so the past participle means pulled or teased out.

clue.text: They're not the best feature on table, next to drink

blocks.note: a table runner is a long decorative cloth
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Something set out on a dining table beside a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNNER is the table cloth and SUP the drink; together they give RUNNERS-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up finish second or behind the winner, so they are the competitors who did not come first.

clue.text: Driver to bargain when going round university on two separate occasions

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the bargain word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: the university letter goes in a second time, at a different spot

explanation.surface: A cabbie haggling over the fare as they circle a campus twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On two separate occasions' means U is inserted twice, at two different places in CHAFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is someone employed to drive a private car or limousine for an employer.

clue.text: Basic arithmetical quantity: youngster's start in education

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal or junior scout

explanation.surface: A child beginning school with simple sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a number multiplied by itself twice, an elementary power taught in school mathematics.

clue.text: To try to get some relief is hard

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Seeking respite is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: relieF IS Hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish for compliments or information is to angle for them, trying indirectly to obtain them.

clue.text: See those people casually hugging large tree

indicators.note: hugging means holding tight in the arms, so the first piece wraps around the next

blocks.note: 'em is the casual form of them

explanation.surface: Look at those folk embracing a big trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an instruction to look, not a cathedral see.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous hardwood once common in British hedgerows, so a type of tree.

clue.text: Men behind roadworthiness test for vehicle

indicators.note: behind means following, so this piece comes second in the answer

blocks.note: the MOT is Britain's annual safety inspection for cars

explanation.surface: Mechanics are lined up after a car's annual inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an everyday British word for a car, an engine-powered road vehicle.

clue.text: Drink and river offering small quantity of liquid

explanation.surface: A cup of tea and a river supply a mere drop of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a single drop of salty fluid from the eye, a tiny amount of moisture.

clue.text: Come out with a lot of money? Not quite, after admitting failure

indicators.note: not quite all means the final letter of the money word is cut off
admitting means letting in, so the shortened word takes the next piece inside it

blocks.note: costing a bomb means very expensive

explanation.surface: Someone emerges rich, or nearly so, after confessing a business flop.
explanation.walkthrough: A bomb is British slang for a large sum of money, as in 'costs a bomb'; 'Come out' is a flower opening, not a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers come out when they bloom, and figuratively a person blossoms when they develop and flourish.

clue.text: Please express anger about male staying inactive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: as in 'do come in', a polite urging
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: A plea not to shout at a man who is just sitting idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant describes something asleep or lying idle, like a volcano or a seed, temporarily not active.
